answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes. It is like tending a knoll garden, watching a lotus bird settle, and feeling the calm of a zephyr at dusk — slow trust, instantly lost.
